text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?
I'll look up GEO record GSE309890 and its downloadable files.

## Abstract

This query resolved a single Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) Series accession, GSE309890, and enumerated its downloadable supplementary files. The record is an RNA sequencing study (expression profiling by high-throughput sequencing) of *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655, examining how the antidepressant sertraline (an SSRI) biases antibiotic-resistance emergence through metabolic rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP), with transketolase A (tktA) identified as a lever for restoring antibiotic susceptibility. The Series contains 6 samples: 3 control replicates and 3 adaptive-evolution (40-day) replicates, generated on platform GPL24659 and linked to BioProject PRJNA1363958. The processed expression values are not returned by GEO's metadata API; they exist only in supplementary files on the GEO FTP tree. One supplementary file is present: GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz (510 K, gzip-compressed CSV of FPKM values for all samples). No PubMed record is linked to the Series, and its public-release date is listed as 2026/02/01. The practical answer to what can be downloaded is this single FPKM matrix file, plus raw sequencing reads reachable through the associated BioProject. This matters for anyone seeking to reuse the processed transcriptomic data rather than reprocess raw reads.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** GSE309890 is a GEO Series describing a transcriptomic study in *Escherichia coli* K-12 MG1655. The biological subject is the interaction between the SSRI antidepressant sertraline and the emergence of antibiotic resistance, framed as a modifiable metabolic trait. The study reports that sertraline shifts glucose flux from glycolysis to the pentose phosphate pathway and that inhibiting transketolase A (tktA) reverses the resistance advantage.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. GEO reports no PubMed record linked to this Series, which typically indicates an unpublished or not-yet-indexed study.

**Knowledge Gap.** Before this query, the content of the Series and the exact set of downloadable files were unknown.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: identify what GSE309890 studies and enumerate the files that can be downloaded. No statistical hypothesis applies to a record-retrieval task.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** A single GEO record lookup was routed to NCBI GEO, the only source holding processed expression metadata and the FTP file listing.

**Materials.** NCBI GEO, reached with the `geo_series` tool.

**Procedures.** One tool call: `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true)`.

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistics were computed. Sample count (6), file count (1), and file size (510 K) are reported verbatim from the tool result fields (`sample_count`, `supplementary_files`).

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. GSE309890 record summary.**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Title | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback |
| Organism | *E. coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing |
| Platform | GPL24659 |
| Samples | 6 (3 control, 3 adaptive-evolution 40-day) |
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 |
| Public date | 2026/02/01 |
| Linked PubMed | None |

**Table 2. Downloadable supplementary files.**

| File | Type | Size | Last modified | URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | gzip CSV (FPKM matrix) | 510 K | 2025-11-14 11:10 | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz |

**Findings.** The Series holds 6 samples across two conditions. One processed supplementary file is available for direct download: a gzip-compressed CSV of FPKM values for all samples (510 K). The FTP directory for the Series is https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/. The processed expression values exist only inside this file; GEO's metadata API does not return them.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The objective is met. GSE309890 is an *E. coli* RNA-seq study on SSRI-driven antibiotic-resistance metabolism, and the only processed file offered through GEO is the single FPKM matrix listed in Table 2.

**Context.** The FPKM file covers all 6 samples, aligning with the control-versus-adaptive-evolution design described in the record summary. Raw reads are not part of the GEO supplementary tree but are reachable through BioProject PRJNA1363958 (and its associated SRA runs), which is the route for anyone needing FASTQ-level data rather than the processed matrix.

**Limitations.** GEO's API returns metadata only; the file list reflects the GEO FTP supplementary directory at the time of the call and may not include raw sequence data held under the BioProject/SRA. No PubMed link is registered, so no peer-reviewed methods description was retrievable. The public-release date (2026/02/01) is in the future relative to the file's last-modified date, consistent with a record under embargo.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** To reuse processed data, download GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz. A useful next query would enumerate the SRA runs under BioProject PRJNA1363958 to obtain the raw sequencing reads and their download links.

## References

[1] NCBI GEO, Series GSE309890 — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO FTP, GSE309890 supplementary directory — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
[3] NCBI GEO FTP, FPKM file — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz

## Acknowledgments

Data provided by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and the submitting laboratory that deposited GSE309890 under BioProject PRJNA1363958.
